name: OCRBench v2
intro: OCRBench v2 是面向大多模态模型的高难度双语视觉文本基准，聚焦单图场景，覆盖 31 个场景、八类 OCR 能力和 23 项任务。公开集包含约 9,500 张图像上的 10,000 条经人工核验的指令—回答；另有 1,500 张独立收集并标注的私有图像用于抗污染排行榜评测。
org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, South China University of Technology, University of Adelaide, ByteDance
build_method: 筛选 81 个数据集, 15 名专业标注员与三人复核门禁, 公开/私有测试集分流
metric: 英文八能力宏平均、中文五能力宏平均（分别按 0–100 报告）
task_type: OCR, 文本定位, 结构解析, 视觉文本推理
eval_feature: 双语, 23项任务, 31个场景, 多指标
scale: 约 9,500 张公开图像上的 10,000 条指令—回答 + 1,500 张私有图像；23 项任务；31 个场景
task_type_en: OCR, text localization, structured parsing, visual text reasoning
build_method_en: Screening 81 Datasets, 15 Professional Annotators with Three-person Review Gate, Public/Private Test Split
intro_en: OCRBench v2 is a high-difficulty bilingual visual-text benchmark for large multimodal models. It focuses on single-image settings and spans 31 scenarios, eight OCR capabilities, and 23 tasks. The public set contains 10,000 human-verified instruction-response rows over about 9,500 images; a separately collected and annotated set of 1,500 private images supports contamination-resistant leaderboard evaluation.
scale_en: 10,000 public instruction-response rows over about 9,500 images + 1,500 private images; 23 tasks; 31 scenarios
metric_en: Separate English 8-capability and Chinese 5-capability macro averages (0–100)

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit fixed on 2026-07-22. The primary construction source is the official NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks final paper at proceedings.neurips.cc; the reviewed 52-page proceedings PDF has SHA-256 2fd3db64a11f51e1892156ccdf14a638c51cf503549be7196a8d77f400600bf2. The linked arXiv:2501.00321v2 PDF is a distinct 45-page artifact with SHA-256 8f4980952029512c53578166f1cf39ad8e6d88203cc1854646ce850b79efac42. Sections 3-5 and Appendices A.2-A.6 of the final paper were checked against both language diagrams. Released behavior was fixed at official Yuliang-Liu/MultimodalOCR commit 86d091f0e3cadd97e98f77ef9f5ecf7e392452c5, current on 2026-07-22. The public ling99/OCRBench_v2 Hugging Face dataset is fixed at revision c7e7cdf23bdb6774661e9b0caf0d9935a42feb8b and reports exactly 10,000 public test rows; the fixed project page repository is 99franklin/ocrbench_v2 commit 982ac76e74994e64f5c5f29b2b659ce56d9a9015. The final paper deliberately limits scope to single-image text-centric tasks rather than multi-page long-context evaluation. The authors manually harvest and screen 81 text-rich academic datasets, add self-annotated and private sources, cover 31 scenarios, and organize 23 tasks under text recognition, text referring, text spotting, relation extraction, element parsing, mathematical calculation, visual text understanding, and knowledge reasoning. Task language coverage is asymmetric rather than universally bilingual. Annotation guidelines require common number and answer variants, all valid alternatives, natural left-to-right then top-to-bottom reading order, and coordinates normalized by image size to 0-1,000. Fifteen professional annotators create instruction-response pairs and coordinates where required, using task contracts such as Markdown, HTML, JSON, and LaTeX. One annotator completes each example, a second reviews it, a third adjudicates disagreement, and an item is excluded if three-way consensus cannot be reached; approximately 1% of annotations are corrected. The public artifact has 10,000 instruction-response rows and about 9,500 images in Table 1; the paper's language statistics partition the rows as 7,400 English and 2,600 Chinese. The private branch has exactly 1,500 text-rich images: 735 manually captured and 765 drawn from unlabeled diverse sources including printed books, e-books, scans, and web content. It is aligned to the public 23-task distribution, human annotated, and checked. The final paper explicitly says this private data will not be released because it is reserved for contamination-resistant testing. Evaluation-code fidelity was checked in fixed eval_scripts/eval.py SHA-256 159ea1fefb6a6edfe700114b7b452817aec44cad1b2afe3d2eebfeb900385271 and get_score.py SHA-256 f3d463e2031b753a4442e46179771667267cbd7b2795075aec5b973863aaf8ed. The released router enumerates 21 English task types and nine Chinese task types. Table and chart parsing use TEDS-based conversions, document parsing uses the released STEDS routine, and parsed key-value structures use F1. Text grounding uses IoU; VQA with position averages content score and IoU equally. Text spotting is summarized as localization in the paper, but the fixed code runs an ICDAR end-to-end spotting evaluator and returns Hmean with an IoU constraint of 0.5, so the diagram records the code boundary instead of calling it plain IoU. Long-reading outputs use the mean of BLEU, METEOR, F1, and one minus normalized edit distance. Character counting uses exact matching; word-count regression uses normalized absolute error, while the fixed implementation additionally zeros results at or below 0.5 similarity. Basic English VQA uses exact options for multiple choice, containment for answers shorter than five words, and thresholded ANLS for longer answers. The Chinese implementation uses its own punctuation-oriented branch, so the diagram avoids claiming one identical tokenizer for both languages. get_score.py first averages item scores within each represented capability, then reports an unweighted macro-average. English covers all eight capabilities; Chinese covers only recognition, extraction, parsing, understanding, and reasoning. The official code and paper tables therefore provide separate English eight-capability and Chinese five-capability results, not one combined bilingual eight-capability score. Availability and rights remain an explicit conflict boundary. The final paper says the private set is withheld, while the current repository news says it was released on 2025-06-21; nevertheless, the fixed public HF mirror contains only the 10,000 public rows and the current project page still labels its tables as private-data leaderboards. The HF card declares MIT, whereas the official OCRBench_v2 README states that data are research-only and not for commercial use, and the benchmark also repackages upstream datasets with their own terms. The diagrams therefore retain partly-public status and do not infer that private labels or uniform commercial rights are available. Formal publication evidence [site-a11x-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 4045×601 (English) and 4045×601 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 4043×599 and 4043×599. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
